Collect the gas in a gas syringe (or over water) and read the volume at regular time intervals.
Flask on a balance with cotton wool in the neck; record the mass as the gas escapes. Good for CO₂, not for H₂.
Time how long a sulfur precipitate takes to hide a cross (thiosulfate + acid); rate ∝ 1/time.

front: Why use cotton wool in the loss-in-mass method?
back: It lets gas escape but stops acid spray leaving the flask.
Steepest at the start, gets less steep as reactants are used up, horizontal when the reaction stops.

front: What decides the final volume of gas?
back: The amount of the limiting reactant. Temperature, concentration of the excess reactant, surface area and catalysts change only the rate.

front: Why does a reaction slow down as it proceeds?
back: Reactants are used up, so there are fewer particles per unit volume and collisions are less frequent.

front: Why is a gas syringe better than collecting CO₂ over water?
back: It is more precise, and carbon dioxide is slightly soluble in water.

front: Rate at a particular time from a graph
back: Draw a tangent at that time; rate = gradient = change in y ÷ change in x.
